domain_label: Test-Time Compute & Structured Reasoning (Reasoning Enhancement subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope covers chain-of-thought, self-consistency, tree/graph-of-thought, best-of-N, verifier-guided search, and token saturation budgeting
core thesis: more structured output enables more intelligence; token budget capped at value-saturation point
practitioner is engineering a production TTC system with real cost and latency constraints
exclusions: pretraining and finetuning internals (only referenced as prerequisite capability)

competency_questions.question: What CoT prompting strategy (zero-shot vs few-shot) is appropriate for the target task and model scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COT_FOUNDATION and SCRATCHPAD_FORMAT define prompt strategy and format

competency_questions.question: How is structured output format designed to enforce reasoning discipline without constraining valid reasoning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCRATCHPAD_FORMAT and STRUCTURED_OUTPUT define format engineering approach

competency_questions.question: How does self-consistency sampling improve accuracy and at what N does it saturate for this task?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_CONSISTENCY defines SC mechanism and saturation via TOKEN_BUDGET

competency_questions.question: When should best-of-N be preferred over self-consistency, and what verifier is required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BEST_OF_N vs SELF_CONSISTENCY conflict edge and CA_01 define decision rule

competency_questions.question: How does tree-of-thought search differ from MCTS and when is each appropriate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TREE_OF_THOUGHT and MCTS_REASONING define search strategies and CA_10 the trade-off

competency_questions.question: What training data and annotation process is required for PRM versus ORM?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORM_VERIFIER and PRM_VERIFIER define annotation requirements

competency_questions.question: How is inference-time verifier reward hacking detected and mitigated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CA_03, EC_03 and DIVERSE_VERIFIER define Goodhart mitigation

competency_questions.question: How is the token saturation budget determined and set for a target task?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOKEN_BUDGET and COMPUTE_SCALING_LAW define measurement and budget-setting process

competency_questions.question: How is MCTS reasoning search configured and what are the key hyperparameters?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MCTS_REASONING defines c_puct, rollout budget, and expansion policy

competency_questions.question: How is inference cost managed across multi-step TTC methods in production?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORCHESTRATION_LATENCY, TOKEN_BUDGET, ADAPTIVE_COMPUTE define cost management

competency_questions.question: How is adaptive compute routing implemented to minimize cost while maintaining accuracy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADAPTIVE_COMPUTE and COMPUTE_SCALING_LAW define routing policy and validation

competency_questions.question: How is benchmark contamination detected and mitigated in TTC evaluation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_CONTAMINATION and EC_07 define detection and mitigation

competency_questions.question: How are offline TTC accuracy gains validated against online task performance before deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ONLINE_OFFLINE_GAP and CA_06 define offline-online validation protocol

competency_questions.question: How is CoT faithfulness assessed and when is a faithfulness audit required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COT_FAITHFULNESS and CA_08 define audit protocol and deployment gate

glossary.definition: intermediate reasoning steps elicited from LLM before final answer
majority vote over multiple independent reasoning chain samples
generate N candidates and return the one scored highest by a verifier
model scoring intermediate reasoning steps rather than only final answers
model scoring final answers as correct or incorrect
point beyond which additional output tokens yield no accuracy improvement
search over partial-solution tree with LLM-evaluated heuristic pruning
Monte Carlo Tree Search balancing exploration/exploitation via UCT over reasoning step trees
optimizing a proxy metric causes it to diverge from the true objective
routing queries to cheap or expensive inference paths based on estimated difficulty

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for TTC reasoning work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Wei et al. 2022 (CoT), Wang et al. 2022 (self-consistency), Yao et al. 2023 (Tree of Thoughts), Cobbe et al. 2021 (verifiers)
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Wei et al. 2022; Wang et al. 2022; Yao et al. 2023; Cobbe et al. 2021
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors grounded in cited literature

nodes.definition: Elicit intermediate reasoning steps from the LLM via few-shot or zero-shot CoT prompts before producing the final answer, improving performance on multi-step tasks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence that direct prompting matches CoT on target task distribution

pros.claim: Substantially improves arithmetic, symbolic, and commonsense reasoning on standard benchmarks
pros.example: GSM8K accuracy jumps >20pp with 8-shot CoT vs direct

pros.claim: Zero-shot CoT ('Let's think step by step') requires no labeled examples
pros.example: Works out-of-box on GPT-4 class models

cons.claim: Requires sufficiently large model; small models produce wrong chains confidently
cons.example: CoT fails below ~7B parameter scale without finetuning

cons.claim: Longer chain increases token cost linearly
cons.example: 8-step chain 8x tokens vs direct answer

failure_modes: plausible-sounding but incorrect chain
verbosity without reasoning gain
acceptance_tests: held-out accuracy exceeds direct-prompting baseline on representative task set
chain steps are causally connected to final answer on manual spot-check
revisit_triggers: model capability upgrade changes optimal prompt style
new task domain with different reasoning structure

nodes.definition: Sample multiple independent reasoning chains at temperature>0 and select the final answer by majority vote (or marginalizing), reducing variance over greedy decoding.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: N sample budget policy changes or latency SLA tightened

pros.claim: Improves accuracy 3-8pp over greedy CoT with N=40 samples on GSM8K
pros.example: Wang et al. 2022 self-consistency results

pros.claim: Model-agnostic; requires no additional training
pros.example: Drop-in over any instruction-following LLM

cons.claim: Inference cost scales linearly with N samples
cons.example: N=40 is 40x single-pass cost

cons.claim: Majority vote can fail if wrong answer cluster dominates
cons.example: Adversarial tasks with systematic bias

failure_modes: consistency illusion: all chains wrong but consistently so
prohibitive cost at production scale
acceptance_tests: majority-voted answer accuracy exceeds single-chain baseline on target task
variance across seeds meets acceptable threshold
revisit_triggers: task answer space changes (open-ended vs closed)

nodes.definition: Decompose reasoning into a tree where nodes are partial solutions; use BFS/DFS with LLM-generated heuristic evaluations to prune branches and find globally coherent solutions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: better search framework (MCTS, A*) shown to dominate on target tasks

pros.claim: Enables backtracking on dead-ends; outperforms linear CoT on planning and puzzle tasks
pros.example: Game of 24: ToT 74% vs CoT 4% (Yao et al. 2023)

pros.claim: Separates proposal and evaluation steps allowing specialized prompts for each
pros.example: Multi-agent decomposition of generate/evaluate

cons.claim: LLM evaluation quality gates search effectiveness; poor evaluator collapses to greedy
cons.example: Weak evaluator on novel domains

cons.claim: Token cost grows multiplicatively with breadth×depth
cons.example: B=5,D=4 tree: 20x single chain

failure_modes: search explosion without tight beam/budget
circular reasoning in self-evaluation
acceptance_tests: BFS/DFS correctly prunes according to LLM evaluator scores
solution found within node budget matches or exceeds greedy CoT quality
revisit_triggers: task structure changes from tree-amenable to sequential

nodes.definition: Extend tree-of-thought to DAG structures allowing reasoning paths to merge, enabling cross-branch aggregation and refinement operations that linear or tree structures cannot express.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: MCTS-based methods shown to dominate on aggregation tasks

pros.claim: Cross-branch merging enables solutions that require combining partial results
pros.example: Sorting: merge sorted sub-lists across branches

pros.claim: Expressive superset of CoT,ToT; subsumes prior paradigms in one framework
pros.example: GoT framework unification

cons.claim: Complex orchestration logic; harder to implement and debug than ToT
cons.example: Aggregate/refine ops require careful prompt engineering

cons.claim: Marginal gain over ToT except on aggregation tasks
cons.example: Overhead not justified for single-answer tasks

failure_modes: merge operation creating logically inconsistent combinations
exploding DAG without pruning
acceptance_tests: aggregate operation produces answer superior to best single branch
operation count stays within budget on representative task
revisit_triggers: task type changes away from aggregation-amenable problems

nodes.definition: Generate N candidate outputs independently; apply a verifier or reward model to score each; return the highest-scoring candidate as the final answer.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: verifier Goodhart failure observed in production

pros.claim: Simple and powerful; strong reward model makes BoN highly effective
pros.example: BoN@256 matches PRM-guided search on MATH

pros.claim: No architectural changes to generator; purely inference-time scaling
pros.example: Drop-in with any base model

cons.claim: Cost scales O(N); ORM/verifier required for quality selection
cons.example: N=256 is 256x single-pass cost

cons.claim: Verifier quality ceiling caps BoN gains; poor verifier selects wrong candidates
cons.example: Goodharted reward model selects verbose over correct

failure_modes: reward hacking: verifier selects wrong answer
N too small to cover solution space
acceptance_tests: best-of-N accuracy exceeds greedy baseline on task benchmark
verifier/RM correlation with human judgment >=0.8

nodes.definition: Train a discriminative model on (problem, candidate-answer) pairs labeled correct/incorrect to score final outputs; used in best-of-N selection and RLHF pipelines.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reward hacking observed or new answer format introduced

pros.claim: Provides differentiable reward signal enabling RLHF and guided search
pros.example: Cobbe et al. 2021 GSM8K verifiers outperform generators

pros.claim: Once trained, scoring is cheap (single forward pass per candidate)
pros.example: Fast inference-time selection signal

cons.claim: Susceptible to reward hacking; model finds high-scoring but wrong solutions
cons.example: ORM scores verbose or confident-sounding wrong answers higher

cons.claim: Requires labeled dataset of correct/incorrect answers which may be scarce
cons.example: Limited coverage on rare problem types

failure_modes: Goodhart: optimizing ORM score diverges from true correctness
distribution shift between train and deployment problems
acceptance_tests: ORM accuracy on held-out correct/incorrect pairs >=0.85
ORM-selected candidate matches ground truth at rate exceeding random baseline
revisit_triggers: new problem types outside training distribution

nodes.definition: Train a step-level reward model that scores each intermediate reasoning step rather than only the final answer; enables fine-grained search guidance and step-level feedback.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: step annotation methodology changes or LLM-labeling shown comparable to human

pros.claim: Step-level feedback guides search more precisely than outcome-only; detects early errors
pros.example: PRM800K training enables MATH step-level supervision

pros.claim: Enables early pruning of incorrect reasoning paths in beam search
pros.example: Fewer wasteful explorations in tree search

cons.claim: Step-level annotation is expensive; requires skilled annotators or LLM distillation
cons.example: Labeling 800K steps costs significant human effort

cons.claim: Process reward may not align with final correctness if steps look correct locally
cons.example: Local step score does not guarantee global solution quality

failure_modes: step-correct but globally-wrong chain rewarded highly
annotation noise corrupts step labels
acceptance_tests: per-step PRM accuracy on held-out annotated steps >=0.80
PRM-guided beam search outperforms ORM-selected BoN on target benchmark

nodes.definition: Apply Monte Carlo Tree Search over reasoning step sequences: select promising partial chains, expand with LLM, evaluate with PRM/ORM rollouts, and backpropagate scores to guide search.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cheaper search method shown to match MCTS on target task class

pros.claim: Balances exploration and exploitation via UCT; avoids greedy-search pitfalls
pros.example: AlphaProof-style MCTS surpasses prior reasoning methods

pros.claim: Online value estimation from rollouts reduces reliance on pre-trained PRM quality
pros.example: Self-play bootstrapping

cons.claim: Very high token budget; each rollout is a full generation
cons.example: MCTS with 1000 rollouts uses orders more compute than CoT

cons.claim: Requires careful tuning of exploration constant and rollout depth
cons.example: c_puct mis-set collapses to greedy or random

failure_modes: exploration-exploitation imbalance leading to premature convergence
rollout noise swamps value signal on short tasks
acceptance_tests: MCTS solution quality exceeds beam-search baseline within same token budget
UCT exploration constant validated via ablation
revisit_triggers: task changes to short-horizon (MCTS overhead not justified)

nodes.definition: Identify the output-length saturation point beyond which additional tokens yield no accuracy gain; set inference token budget at this point to maximize cost-efficiency.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model retrained or task distribution changes materially

pros.claim: Capping at saturation point can reduce inference cost 30-60% with negligible accuracy loss
pros.example: Saturation analysis on GSM8K shows plateau at ~500 tokens

pros.claim: Exposes structured vs verbose reasoning trade-off quantitatively
pros.example: Empirical curve informs prompt design decisions

cons.claim: Saturation point is task- and model-specific; must be re-measured after model updates
cons.example: Saturation point measured on GPT-4 may not hold for different models

cons.claim: Premature budget cap degrades performance on rare hard instances
cons.example: Long-tail hard problems may need full chain

failure_modes: setting budget from wrong model/task combination
missing long-tail performance degradation
acceptance_tests: saturation curve measured on representative task sample with N>=100 queries
budget set at p95 saturation point preserves >=99% of max accuracy

nodes.definition: Design the intermediate-work format (markdown sections, numbered steps, XML tags, code blocks) that structures the model's scratch space to enforce reasoning discipline and enable reliable parsing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: parser failure rate exceeds 5% in production

pros.claim: Structured format reduces parsing failures and enables programmatic extraction of reasoning steps
pros.example: XML-tagged steps parseable with regex without LLM re-call

pros.claim: Enforces discipline: model less likely to skip steps when format mandates them
pros.example: Mandatory numbered steps catch omissions

cons.claim: Over-constraining format may cut off valid reasoning styles
cons.example: Rigid format hurts creative problem-solving

cons.claim: Model may satisfy format constraints while producing vacuous content
cons.example: Format compliance != reasoning quality

failure_modes: format compliance without semantic content
parser brittleness on edge cases
acceptance_tests: parser extracts all required sections on >=95% of outputs without error
format-compliant outputs show accuracy improvement over free-form baseline

nodes.definition: Run beam search over reasoning steps where beam scoring at each expansion step uses a trained verifier (PRM) rather than generator log-probabilities, enabling quality-guided exploration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: PRM recalibrated or beam search replaced by MCTS

pros.claim: PRM guidance substantially outperforms likelihood-scored beam search on mathematical reasoning
pros.example: Lightman et al. PRM beam search results on MATH

pros.claim: Beam width B tunable for cost-quality trade-off without retraining
pros.example: Flexible scaling of search compute

cons.claim: PRM quality bottleneck: miscalibrated PRM degrades over likelihood scoring
cons.example: PRM trained on narrow domain generalizes poorly

cons.claim: Beam search may still be myopic on very long chains; MCTS preferable
cons.example: Long-horizon problems: greedy step scoring misses global coherence

failure_modes: PRM-guided beam converges to locally-good but globally-wrong chains
beam collapse to near-duplicate solutions
acceptance_tests: PRM-guided beam@B=8 accuracy exceeds likelihood-beam@B=8 on target benchmark
beam diversity measured by unique leaf count meets minimum threshold

nodes.definition: Prompt the model to critique its own draft answer, identify errors, and produce an improved revision over multiple rounds, enabling error correction without external supervision.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: self-critique reliability drops below 50% on target task class

pros.claim: Improves code, math, and writing quality without external feedback
pros.example: Self-Refine paper shows consistent gains on code optimization tasks

pros.claim: Critique-then-refine loop enables principled error localization
pros.example: Model explicitly states what is wrong before fixing

cons.claim: Model may repeat same error or hallucinate new errors in critique phase
cons.example: Self-critique reliability degrades on factual tasks

cons.claim: Convergence not guaranteed; may oscillate between versions
cons.example: Refinement loop runs max_rounds without improvement signal

failure_modes: self-sycophancy: model agrees its first answer was fine
critique hallucination: inventing errors not present
acceptance_tests: refinement accuracy monotonically improves or stabilizes within 3 rounds
critique identifies genuine error on >=60% of incorrect drafts
revisit_triggers: task switches to factual QA where hallucination risk high

nodes.definition: Break complex problems into ordered sub-goals or sub-tasks before solving; includes least-to-most prompting, plan-then-execute, and modular decomposition patterns.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sub-goal granularity shown suboptimal by ablation

pros.claim: Least-to-most prompting improves compositional generalization on SCAN and COGS
pros.example: Zhou et al. 2022 least-to-most prompting results

pros.claim: Enables parallel execution of independent sub-tasks reducing wall-clock time
pros.example: Independent branches parallelized in orchestration

cons.claim: Decomposition error cascades: wrong sub-goal produces wrong downstream answers
cons.example: Incorrect first sub-goal taints entire chain

cons.claim: Over-decomposition adds overhead without accuracy gain on simple tasks
cons.example: Trivial tasks fragmented into unnecessary steps

failure_modes: decomposition error cascade
over-decomposition overhead on simple tasks
acceptance_tests: assembled answer from sub-goals matches direct CoT quality on >=90% of complex tasks
decomposition boundary validated by human expert on representative sample
revisit_triggers: new task type with different decomposition grammar

nodes.definition: Apply weighted combinations of ORM, PRM, format compliance, and constraint-satisfaction signals to score candidates; tune signal weights for the target task without retraining the generator.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: signal weight ablation shows one signal dominates and others redundant

pros.claim: Combines complementary signals; PRM and ORM errors partially uncorrelated
pros.example: Ensemble reduces single-model Goodhart risk

pros.claim: Weight tuning at inference time is cheap vs retraining
pros.example: Grid search over 3-4 weights feasible in hours

cons.claim: Weight misspecification can amplify rather than cancel individual model errors
cons.example: Wrong weight vector overweights hallucination-prone signal

cons.claim: Composite signal harder to interpret and debug than single reward
cons.example: Diagnosis unclear when composite score wrong

failure_modes: weight misspecification amplifying errors
composite metric masking individual failures
acceptance_tests: composite-scored candidates outperform single-signal selection on target benchmark
ablation shows each signal contributes positively to composite

nodes.definition: Empirically measure how task accuracy scales with inference compute (tokens, N samples, search nodes); fit power-law or saturation curves to inform deployment budget decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model update or new task class introduced

pros.claim: Informs optimal compute allocation across sampling, search, and chain length dimensions
pros.example: Identifies whether to spend budget on N or chain depth

pros.claim: Power-law fit enables extrapolation to higher compute before incurring full cost
pros.example: Cheaply predicts gain from 10x compute increase

cons.claim: Scaling behavior is task- and model-specific; curves measured on one model may not transfer
cons.example: Scaling measured on GPT-4 does not predict smaller models

cons.claim: Measurement requires large benchmark runs which are expensive
cons.example: Hundreds of GPU-hours for comprehensive scaling study

failure_modes: overfitting scaling curve to narrow benchmark
extrapolating beyond measured range
acceptance_tests: scaling curve R^2 >= 0.9 on held-out compute budget points
saturation threshold estimate within 10% across 3 independent runs
revisit_triggers: new compute paradigm (cached KV, speculative decoding)

nodes.definition: Assess whether generated reasoning chains are causal explanations of model decisions versus post-hoc rationalizations; measure faithfulness via intervention tests and causal probing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: faithfulness score drops below threshold in production audit

pros.claim: Identifies whether chain is merely decorative vs genuinely causal
pros.example: Turpin et al. 2023: CoT chains unfaithful to model internals on biased prompts

pros.claim: Flags cases where model answer changes on reordering steps; reveals brittle reasoning
pros.example: Counterfactual step-removal reveals causal dependency

cons.claim: Faithfulness measures themselves are imperfect and contested
cons.example: No consensus protocol for causal CoT attribution

cons.claim: Unfaithful chains may still produce correct answers; faithfulness != accuracy
cons.example: High faithfulness required only for high-stakes or regulated applications

failure_modes: low faithfulness undetected in production
audit methodology not matched to task type
acceptance_tests: intervention test shows >=70% of chain steps causally necessary for correct answer
faithfulness score stable across 3 prompt variations
revisit_triggers: model update changes internal reasoning mechanism
regulated deployment triggers stricter audit requirement

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate benchmark contamination where TTC-improved model performance reflects memorized test instances rather than genuine reasoning; enforce held-out contamination-free evaluation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training data updated or benchmark widely published online

pros.claim: Prevents reporting inflated gains driven by memorization rather than reasoning
pros.example: n-gram overlap scan on GSM8K training data

pros.claim: Held-out clean benchmark gives trustworthy compute-scaling measurements
pros.example: Ensures scaling curves reflect genuine generalization

cons.claim: Contamination detection is heuristic; n-gram overlap misses paraphrased contamination
cons.example: Paraphrased benchmark questions evade n-gram filter

cons.claim: Restricting to clean benchmarks reduces evaluation set size
cons.example: Smaller clean set increases variance in accuracy estimates

failure_modes: false-clean benchmark inflating measured TTC gains
Goodhart: optimizing reported benchmark metric not generalizable reasoning
acceptance_tests: contamination rate below 5% on training/benchmark overlap scan
held-out clean benchmark accuracy consistent with contaminated benchmark within 2pp
revisit_triggers: training data updated or new benchmark adopted

nodes.definition: Profile and control the wall-clock latency and dollar cost of multi-step TTC methods (ToT, MCTS, BoN) in production; implement caching, batching, and early-exit policies to meet SLA.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: hardware or pricing change invalidates cost model

pros.claim: KV-cache sharing across BoN candidates reduces redundant prefill cost
pros.example: Shared prompt prefix cached once for N completions

pros.claim: Early-exit policy avoids full search when high-confidence answer found quickly
pros.example: Confidence threshold exits beam search at step 3 of 10

cons.claim: Caching adds infrastructure complexity and cache-invalidation bugs
cons.example: Stale cached prefix gives wrong context after prompt change

cons.claim: Early exit may prematurely stop on hard problems where confidence is misleadingly high
cons.example: Confident wrong intermediate state triggers early exit

failure_modes: SLA breach under burst traffic
early exit triggered on hard problems producing wrong answer
acceptance_tests: p99 latency within SLA under simulated peak load
cost per query within budget at measured accuracy level

nodes.definition: Combine structurally diverse verifiers (ORM, PRM, rule-based checker, symbolic solver) via ensemble voting or learned meta-ranker to reduce individual verifier Goodhart failure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any component verifier shown correlated with another

pros.claim: Diverse verifiers have partially uncorrelated errors; ensemble reduces joint failure rate
pros.example: ORM and symbolic checker disagree on structurally different errors

pros.claim: Disagreement signal identifies ambiguous candidates for human review
pros.example: High disagreement triggers escalation to human annotator

cons.claim: Ensemble requires maintaining multiple verifier inference pipelines
cons.example: Ops overhead of 4 verifier models vs 1

cons.claim: Meta-ranker training requires labeled ensemble-disagreement examples
cons.example: Bootstrapping meta-ranker is expensive

failure_modes: correlated verifier errors defeat ensemble benefit
meta-ranker overfit to training disagreement patterns
acceptance_tests: ensemble accuracy exceeds best individual verifier by >=2pp on target benchmark
disagreement signal precision >=0.7 on candidate ambiguity

nodes.definition: Route easy queries to cheap inference (direct answer or short CoT) and hard queries to expensive TTC methods (BoN, ToT, MCTS) using a difficulty classifier to minimize cost at target accuracy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: difficulty classifier accuracy drops below threshold in production

pros.claim: Large cost savings: 50-80% of queries are easy and need only direct answer
pros.example: Difficulty routing on math benchmarks saves >60% compute vs uniform BoN@32

pros.claim: Enables serving higher TTC quality within fixed compute budget
pros.example: Frees budget from easy queries for hard ones

cons.claim: Difficulty classifier errors misroute hard queries to cheap path
cons.example: Easy-labeled hard query gets wrong answer at low cost

cons.claim: Routing adds latency and infrastructure complexity
cons.example: Extra classifier call adds ~10ms overhead per query

failure_modes: difficulty mis-classification routing hard queries to cheap path
classifier distribution shift over time
acceptance_tests: difficulty classifier F1 >= 0.80 on held-out difficulty-labeled query set
adaptive routing accuracy matches oracle-routed within 2pp at 30% lower cost
revisit_triggers: model capability update changes difficulty landscape

nodes.definition: Enforce structured generation (JSON schema, grammar-constrained decoding, function-call schemas) on reasoning outputs to guarantee machine-parseable intermediate and final results.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: parse error rate exceeds 1% in production

pros.claim: Eliminates output parsing failures in downstream pipeline; enables deterministic extraction
pros.example: JSON-mode outputs parse without regex heuristics

pros.claim: Grammar-constrained decoding ensures format validity at generation time with near-zero overhead
pros.example: Outlines library adds <5% latency on typical schemas

cons.claim: Schema constraints may reduce generation quality by excluding valid token sequences
cons.example: Tight JSON schema may prevent model expressing uncertainty naturally

cons.claim: Schema design requires careful alignment with task semantics; wrong schema invalidates outputs
cons.example: Mismatched schema causes valid reasoning to be flagged as invalid

failure_modes: schema too restrictive excludes valid reasoning
schema mismatch causes silent correctness failures
acceptance_tests: parse success rate >=99% in production
schema-constrained accuracy matches unconstrained within 1pp on target task

nodes.definition: Define and implement the evaluation metric suite for TTC systems: accuracy, pass@k, majority@k, coverage, cost-normalized accuracy, and latency-accuracy Pareto curves.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production cost model changes or new TTC method deployed

pros.claim: pass@k and majority@k expose compute-accuracy trade-off missed by single-pass accuracy
pros.example: Chen et al. 2021: pass@k critical for code generation evaluation

pros.claim: Cost-normalized accuracy enables apples-to-apples comparison across TTC methods
pros.example: Prevents expensive methods winning only due to higher compute

cons.claim: Multiple metrics create evaluation complexity; conflicting metric results require judgment
cons.example: pass@1 vs majority@40 optimization objectives diverge

cons.claim: Latency measurement requires production-representative infrastructure to be valid
cons.example: Lab latency numbers mislead production capacity planning

failure_modes: metric overfitting: optimizing easy metric ignores hard one
latency measured on wrong infrastructure
acceptance_tests: all metrics computed on same fixed benchmark and model version
cost-normalized accuracy computed using actual inference cost not FLOPs proxy
revisit_triggers: new TTC method introduces new metric dimension

nodes.definition: Validate that offline TTC accuracy gains (benchmark) transfer to online task performance; identify and close gaps caused by distribution shift, latency constraints, or user behavior differences.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: online metric diverges from offline by >5pp

pros.claim: Catches cases where offline gains do not transfer due to distribution mismatch
pros.example: CoT improves GSM8K offline but user query distribution differs

pros.claim: A/B test provides causal estimate of TTC benefit under real user conditions
pros.example: Online experiment isolates TTC effect from confounders

cons.claim: Online A/B tests are slow and expensive; minimum detectable effect requires large traffic
cons.example: Small effect size needs weeks of traffic for significance

cons.claim: Latency constraints in production may force reduced TTC budget vs offline evaluation
cons.example: Production BoN@4 vs offline BoN@32 gap

failure_modes: offline-online gap misattributed to distribution shift when actually latency-induced
premature deployment on offline gains that do not transfer
acceptance_tests: offline-online accuracy gap quantified and root-cause attributed
online A/B shows statistically significant improvement before full deployment

edges.resolution_rule: Prefer BoN when verifier available; SC when only answer labels exist; cost budget determines choice
MCTS high latency must be constrained by SLA; choose beam search if p99 budget exceeded
Self-refinement preferred when critique signal is reliable; SC preferred when refinement self-corrupts; measure on task

conflict_axes.name: accuracy_vs_cost
conflict_axes.description: Higher TTC compute (BoN, MCTS, ToT) improves accuracy but multiplies inference cost and latency
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use adaptive routing: cheap path for easy queries, expensive TTC for hard queries within SLA

conflict_axes.name: chain_length_vs_saturation
conflict_axes.description: Longer chains improve multi-step accuracy up to a saturation point; beyond it, cost increases without gain
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Measure saturation curve; cap at p95 saturation token count for target task

conflict_axes.name: verifier_quality_vs_goodhart
conflict_axes.description: Stronger verifiers improve selection quality but enable reward hacking when over-optimized
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Ensemble diverse verifiers; monitor for Goodhart drift via held-out correctness labels

conflict_axes.name: search_depth_vs_myopia
conflict_axes.description: Deeper search (MCTS) reduces myopia but step-level reward signals may still be locally misleading
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use rollout-based value estimation in MCTS to reduce step-level myopia

conflict_axes.name: structured_format_vs_reasoning_freedom
conflict_axes.description: Structured scratchpad enforces discipline but may constrain valid reasoning styles
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use minimal-constraint format (numbered steps) rather than rigid schema for open-ended reasoning

conflict_axes.name: offline_benchmark_vs_online_reality
conflict_axes.description: Offline TTC gains on benchmarks do not always transfer to online user task performance
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Always run online A/B before full deployment of new TTC method; measure offline-online correlation

conflict_axes.name: self_refinement_vs_sycophancy
conflict_axes.description: Self-refinement can improve quality but also exhibit sycophancy where model validates its own errors
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Use external verifier or SC to override self-critique on high-stakes tasks

conflict_axes.name: chain_faithfulness_vs_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Faithful chains are harder to generate; accuracy-optimized chains may be post-hoc rationalizations
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Accept faithfulness-accuracy trade-off in non-regulated contexts; require faithfulness audit in regulated deployments

conflict_axes.name: annotation_cost_vs_verifier_quality
conflict_axes.description: Higher-quality PRM requires expensive step-level human annotation; reducing annotation degrades PRM
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Bootstrap PRM with LLM-labeled steps then refine with human annotation on hard cases only

conflict_axes.name: tree_search_vs_beam_search
conflict_axes.description: Tree/MCTS search explores broadly but costs multiplicatively; beam search is cheaper but greedier
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: Default to PRM-guided beam for cost-constrained production; use MCTS only on highest-value long-horizon tasks

edge_cases.description: Model produces confident-sounding incorrect CoT chain that consistently fools SC majority vote
edge_cases.trigger: all N samples agree on wrong answer due to systematic model bias
edge_cases.mitigation: Use external verifier (ORM) rather than SC on factual tasks; diversify temperature

edge_cases.description: PRM assigns high step scores to locally-plausible but globally-wrong chains
edge_cases.trigger: PRM trained on different problem distribution than deployment
edge_cases.mitigation: Measure PRM step accuracy on target domain; add ORM final-answer check

edge_cases.description: BoN reward model Goodharts: selects verbose or confidence-signaling wrong answers
edge_cases.trigger: ORM training distribution over-represents confident-sounding correct answers
edge_cases.mitigation: Calibrate ORM on adversarial correct-sounding-wrong examples; use diverse verifier ensemble

edge_cases.description: Token saturation curve measured on easy benchmark does not apply to long-tail hard queries
edge_cases.trigger: Benchmark task distribution excludes rare hard multi-hop problems
edge_cases.mitigation: Stratify saturation measurement by difficulty tier; set budget at hard-query saturation

edge_cases.description: Self-refinement loop hallucinating new errors in otherwise correct draft
edge_cases.trigger: Model critique phase invents non-existent errors when draft is already correct
edge_cases.mitigation: Add external correctness check before allowing refinement to proceed; limit max rounds

edge_cases.description: Tree-of-thought search explodes in branching factor on unstructured text generation tasks
edge_cases.trigger: No natural step decomposition; every token is a branch decision
edge_cases.mitigation: Restrict ToT to tasks with natural step decomposition; use SC or BoN for fluency tasks

edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination inflates TTC scaling measurements on widely-published datasets
edge_cases.trigger: Training data includes test set n-grams from GSM8K or MATH
edge_cases.mitigation: Scan training data for benchmark overlap; use contamination-free holdout sets

edge_cases.description: Adaptive compute router mis-classifies hard queries as easy under distribution shift
edge_cases.trigger: Query topic distribution shifts away from router training distribution
edge_cases.mitigation: Monitor router confidence calibration in production; fall back to expensive path on low-confidence routing

edge_cases.description: KV-cache sharing for BoN introduces stale context when prompt changes without cache invalidation
edge_cases.trigger: Prompt template updated but cached prefix not invalidated
edge_cases.mitigation: Version-tag all cached prefixes; invalidate cache on any prompt template change

edge_cases.description: MCTS rollout budget exhausted on long-horizon tasks before any complete solution found
edge_cases.trigger: Rollout depth insufficient for problem length; budget set from shorter problems
edge_cases.mitigation: Set rollout depth budget from p95 problem length in target task distribution

edge_cases.description: Structured output schema too restrictive causes model to truncate or corrupt reasoning
edge_cases.trigger: JSON schema disallows multi-sentence reasoning field; model shortens chain
edge_cases.mitigation: Use lenient string fields for reasoning steps; apply schema validation only on final answer fields

edge_cases.description: CoT faithfulness audit detects post-hoc rationalization but accuracy is unaffected; deployment decision unclear
edge_cases.trigger: Faithfulness score low but task accuracy high; regulated deployment context
edge_cases.mitigation: Separate faithfulness requirement by deployment context: required for regulated, optional for accuracy-only tasks

workflow.action: Define reasoning task scope and choose CoT prompt strategy (zero-shot vs few-shot)
workflow.gate: accuracy on dev set exceeds no-CoT baseline

workflow.action: Design structured scratchpad format and validate parser
Establish evaluation metric suite (accuracy, pass@k, cost-normalized accuracy)
workflow.gate: metrics computed correctly on reference outputs

workflow.action: Run self-consistency sampling and measure SC accuracy vs greedy at multiple N values
workflow.gate: SC@N>1 beats greedy on target task

workflow.action: Train ORM on correct/incorrect answer pairs; validate calibration
Evaluate best-of-N with ORM; measure accuracy vs N scaling curve
workflow.gate: BoN@N accuracy exceeds SC@N at same compute budget

workflow.action: If higher quality needed: annotate step-level labels and train PRM
workflow.gate: PRM step accuracy >=0.80 on held-out annotated steps

workflow.action: Run PRM-guided beam search and compare to BoN at same compute
workflow.gate: PRM-beam beats BoN on target benchmark

workflow.action: Measure token saturation curve; set inference token budget
Fit TTC compute scaling law; decide whether to deploy ToT/MCTS for high-value hard queries
Build adaptive compute router; validate routing accuracy and cost savings
Profile orchestration latency; configure caching and early exit; validate SLA
workflow.gate: p99 latency within SLA under peak load

dominance_rules.rule: PRM-guided beam search dominates ORM-only BoN at same compute budget on multi-step mathematical reasoning
dominance_rules.condition: task has well-defined reasoning steps; PRM trained on domain

dominance_rules.rule: Adaptive compute routing dominates uniform compute allocation at any accuracy target when query difficulty variance is high
Token saturation budget dominates uncapped generation when task accuracy plateau is confirmed
dominance_rules.condition: saturation curve measured on representative sample
exceptions: long-tail hard queries requiring full chain

dominance_rules.rule: Diverse verifier ensemble dominates single ORM when Goodhart failure observed in production
SC majority vote dominates greedy decoding when temperature sampling is cheap and N>=8
exceptions: very long chain where N>=8 is prohibitive

dominance_rules.rule: Benchmark contamination guard must pass before publishing any TTC scaling measurement
dominance_rules.condition: training data not provably disjoint from benchmark
exceptions: benchmark newly created and training data predates it

dominance_rules.rule: Online A/B test dominates offline-only evaluation for deployment decisions on user-facing products
dominance_rules.condition: sufficient traffic for minimum detectable effect
exceptions: pre-launch product with no live traffic

dominance_rules.rule: PRM dominates ORM as search guide for long-horizon tasks where early errors are hard to detect at end
dominance_rules.condition: PRM trained on target domain; task horizon >5 steps

dominance_rules.rule: MCTS dominates beam search on tasks requiring global coherence across many steps when compute budget allows
dominance_rules.condition: rollout budget 100x single chain; task is combinatorially hard
exceptions: SLA too tight for MCTS overhead

dominance_rules.rule: Structured output enforcement dominates free-form output when downstream parsing reliability is required
exceptions: creative or open-ended tasks where schema overly restrictive

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not tune token budget before measuring saturation curve on representative task sample
anti_rework_rules.prevents: premature capping that degrades hard-query accuracy

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy ORM-based BoN in production without Goodhart stress-test
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: launch BEST_OF_N without ORM adversarial evaluation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not report TTC scaling results without contamination scan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inflated benchmark numbers from memorized test instances
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: publish COMPUTE_SCALING_LAW results without BENCHMARK_CONTAMINATION check

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not annotate step-level PRM labels before ORM baseline is validated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wasted annotation effort if ORM already sufficient
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: start PRM_VERIFIER annotation before BEST_OF_N with ORM evaluated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy adaptive compute router without difficulty classifier validation on held-out queries
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mis-routing hard queries to cheap path
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: launch ADAPTIVE_COMPUTE without router F1 >=0.80 validation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize scratchpad format before running parse success test on model output samples
anti_rework_rules.prevents: parser brittleness discovered late in deployment
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: lock SCRATCHPAD_FORMAT before parse success rate measured

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy MCTS reasoning in production without SLA validation under peak load
anti_rework_rules.prevents: latency SLA breach from MCTS rollout overhead

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not use self-consistency as sole verifier on factual knowledge tasks
anti_rework_rules.prevents: consistent-wrong-answer failure from correlated model bias
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: deploy SELF_CONSISTENCY without ORM backup on factual tasks

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize PRM without per-step accuracy measurement on domain-matched held-out annotations
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: deploy PRM_VERIFIER without domain-matched step accuracy report

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not launch new TTC method without offline-online gap analysis
anti_rework_rules.prevents: offline benchmark gains that fail to transfer to user tasks
anti_rework_rules.blocked_action: promote new TTC method to production without ONLINE_OFFLINE_GAP validation

iteration_protocol.trigger: offline TTC accuracy gain does not replicate in online A/B
iteration_protocol.action: run ONLINE_OFFLINE_GAP root-cause analysis; check distribution shift, latency constraints, SC vs user task format

iteration_protocol.trigger: ORM Goodhart failure detected (high ORM score but low correctness)
iteration_protocol.action: collect adversarial examples; retrain ORM; add DIVERSE_VERIFIER ensemble

iteration_protocol.trigger: token saturation budget causes accuracy regression on hard queries
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure saturation by difficulty tier; set tier-specific budgets

iteration_protocol.trigger: PRM step accuracy below 0.80 on target domain
iteration_protocol.action: collect more domain-matched step annotations; consider LLM-distillation to bootstrap

iteration_protocol.trigger: CoT faithfulness score below threshold in regulated deployment audit
iteration_protocol.action: redesign CoT prompt to encourage causal chains; re-run faithfulness audit

iteration_protocol.trigger: adaptive compute router F1 drops below 0.75 in production
iteration_protocol.action: retrain difficulty classifier on recent production query distribution
switch to contamination-free benchmark; re-measure TTC scaling curves
reduce rollout budget or beam width; fall back to PRM-guided beam search; re-validate SLA

iteration_protocol.trigger: self-refinement accuracy regresses vs single-pass baseline
iteration_protocol.action: diagnose self-critique quality; add external verifier gate before allowing refinement

priority_rationale: COT_FOUNDATION is the prerequisite for all TTC methods. SCRATCHPAD_FORMAT and EVAL_TTC_METRICS must be locked early to enable structured iteration. SELF_CONSISTENCY and TOKEN_BUDGET provide cheap accuracy and cost gains before expensive verifier training. ORM then PRM verifiers unlock guided search. COMPUTE_SCALING_LAW informs ADAPTIVE_COMPUTE routing. TREE_OF_THOUGHT and MCTS are high-compute high-complexity and deferred until verifiers are validated. DIVERSE_VERIFIER and REWARD_SHAPING are refinements. Audit nodes (FAITHFULNESS, CONTAMINATION, ONLINE_OFFLINE_GAP) are gating nodes for deployment.
